newsitem.title: USA: Legislation advances plan for Alaska gas sales.
newsitem.headline: Legislation advances plan for Alaska gas sales.

text.p: A bill passed by the state legislature will help make deals spurring commercialization of Alaska's vast North Slope gas reserves more acceptable to the public, Gov. Tony Knowles said Thursday.

The legislation, which was sponsored by the governor, authorizes him to set up a gas commercialization team comprising three of his cabinet members. The team was directed to report back next year on ways to encourage development of a market for natural gas sales.

Knowles, a Democrat, said his administration could have begun negotiating tax and royalty inducements without passage of the bill, but legislative authorization makes the state seem more serious to oil and gas producers and allowed the public a chance to weigh in on the issue.

"What we're discussing with the producers potentially is a fundamental change in financial relationship between the state and producers, and I wanted a legislative approval to go ahead with that," he said.
"When you go to negotiate, you do so in good faith. And I wanted to make sure that I had the public and legislative support in doing that," he said.
The state was seeking to sell its 35 trillion cubic feet of North Slope gas, but delivering the gas to market would require construction of new pipeline estimated to cost up to $15 billion.
Alaska envisions shipping liquified North Slope natural gas from the port of Valdez to Asian markets, he said.
